title: Judge-labeled invalid coding traces were longer in two related models
summary: Code-generation reasoning traces labeled invalid by a model-judge ensemble averaged 17,163 tokens for DeepSeek-R1-0528, compared with 7,102 for valid-labeled traces. Its distilled 8B variant showed the same direction. These labels concern reasoning coherence and are explicitly distinct from whether the final code passes functional tests.

source_review.scope: v1 task/model setup, trace taxonomy and §§4.1–4.2 differences by outcome

evidence.tested: Researchers collected traces under matched prompting and decoding. Three model judges each rated trace validity three times; confidence-weighted votes labeled high-confidence cases and two human annotators adjudicated the remainder. The reported length contrast groups these trace-validity labels, not final code correctness.
evidence.unknown: Validity judgments include coherence and unnecessary detours, which may themselves relate to trace length; the contrast does not establish a causal effect of long reasoning or a functional-code failure rate. The models share a lineage, selected complete traces exclude incomplete or unparsable responses, and verbal traces need not faithfully reflect internal reasoning.
evidence.ai_role: DeepSeek R1 models generated traces; DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Flash and GLM-5.1 judged their validity, while learned semantic annotators classified reasoning actions.
